stories.title: Millennium Bank Debuts Revitalized Bridgeport Banking Center
stories.excerpt: Millennium Bank has officially opened its newly renovated Bridgeport banking center. Following its January 2025 acquisition of Pulaski Savings Bank, Millennium Bank invested in the historic property at 3156 S. Morgan Street, rebuilt branch operations and expanded its presence in Chicago. A centerpiece of the reopening is a new 120-foot exterior mural by Chicago artist Jeff Zimmerman, commissioned by Millennium Bank to celebrate Bridgeport’s history, character and community. Pulaski Savings Bank operated in Bridgeport since 1890 before the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation closed it. Millennium Bank subsequently acquired the institution, preserving a neighborhood banking presence. Founded in 2007, Millennium Bank has grown to nearly $1 billion in assets and has become one of Illinois’ leading Small Business Administration lenders for hospitality, commercial real estate, and multifamily housing. Over the past decade, the bank has funded approximately $350 million in loans, with a focus on minority business owners and real estate developers. The post Millennium Bank Debuts Revitalized Bridgeport Banking Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Millennium Bank acquired Pulaski Savings Bank (Chicago), reopened Bridgeport branch Jan 2025
Bank has $1B assets, funded ~$350M in loans over decade, focuses on multifamily
Community banking presence restored in historically underserved Chicago neighborhood
stories.summary: Millennium Bank reopened a renovated banking center in Chicago's Bridgeport after acquiring failed Pulaski Savings Bank in January 2025. The SBA lender, with nearly $1 billion in assets, has deployed approximately $350 million in loans over the past decade with a focus on minority business owners and multifamily developers. The 2022-era building renovation and neighborhood reinvestment signal stabilizing community credit access.
stories.impact: Restored local lending capacity in Chicago's Bridgeport may ease financing for smaller multifamily developers and value-add operators in the submarket, particularly those underserved by national lenders. Improved credit availability could support modest development and renovation activity in a historically under-capitalized area.

stories.title: JLL Arranges $276M Refi for Newport Beach Seniors Communities
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged $276 million in refinancing for Vivante Newport Center and Vivante Newport Mesa, a two-property seniors housing portfolio in Newport Beach. Senior managing director Greg Brown, assisted by senior managing director Aaron Rosenzweig worked on behalf of the borrower, an affiliate of Nexus Development, to secure two uncrossed loans for the portfolio. A $140-million loan was arranged for Newport Center through a national bank and a $136-million agency financing was arranged for Newport Mesa. According to JLL, the Newport Center financing is one of the largest loans per unit in the seniors housing industry’s history. Vivante Newport Center was built in 2022 and is a luxury six-story community offering 99 units of independent living, assisted living and memory care units. Vivante Newport Mesa opened in two phases in 2013 and 2020 and offers 296 units of independent living, assisted living and memory care. The post JLL Arranges $276M Refi for Newport Beach Seniors Communities appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Nexus Development affiliate refi'd $276M (two senior housing properties, Newport Beach, CA)
$140M loan for 99-unit Newport Center = ~$1.4M per unit, top-tier seniors metric
Portfolio mix: 99 units (2022 luxury) + 296 units (2013/2020) across two properties
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $276 million in refinancing for Vivante Newport Center (99 units, opened 2022) and Vivante Newport Mesa (296 units, opened 2013/2020) in Newport Beach, California. Bank financing ($140M) for Newport Center achieved approximately $1.4 million per unit, among the largest per-unit senior housing financings on record. The deal signals strong capital appetite and pricing power for new, luxury senior housing assets in affluent coastal markets.
stories.impact: Validates aggressive per-unit debt sizing for newly-built, luxury senior housing in trophy Orange County markets, supporting continued investment in upscale independent/assisted living. Strong refinancing at scale suggests institutional lenders remain confident in senior housing fundamentals despite broader rate environment.

stories.title: Northmarq Arranges Sale of St. Louis Metro Multifamily Property
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s St. Louis Investment Sales team, led by Dominic Martinez, Parker Stewart, Alex Malzone and Charlie McKee, successfully arranged the sale of Whisper Hollow Apartments, a 315-unit garden-style multifamily community located at 12430 Whisper Hollow Dr. in Maryland Heights, Missouri. Northmarq represented the seller, Banner Real Estate Group, in the transaction. The buyer is Monarch Investment and Management Group. “We were extremely pleased to collect 21 written offers, especially for 50-year-old product in St. Louis,” Martinez said. “The competitive bidding process helped create for an extremely smooth transaction which is imperative given today’s volatile market conditions.” Built in 1976 and renovated in 2018, Whisper Hollow sits on roughly 14.48 acres and features 13 three-story buildings. Floorplans include studio, one- and two-bedrooms. Apartments feature updated kitchens and bathrooms, stainless steel appliances, private entrances, hardwood-style floors, private patio or balcony, ceiling fans, energy-efficient doors and windows, and high-speed internet. It is roughly 20 miles from downtown St. Louis. The post Northmarq Arranges Sale of St. Louis Metro Multifamily Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Whisper Hollow Apartments (315 units, Maryland Heights, MO) sold by Banner to Monarch Group
Built 1976, renovated 2018, garden-style; deal generated 21 written offers
Broker noted competitive bidding despite 50-year vintage in volatile market
stories.summary: Northmarq arranged the sale of Whisper Hollow Apartments, a 315-unit garden-style community in Maryland Heights, Missouri, built in 1976 and renovated in 2018. The asset attracted 21 written offers and was purchased by Monarch Investment and Management Group. Strong competitive interest in a 50-year-old product signals renewed investor appetite for stabilized, well-maintained garden-style multifamily in St. Louis suburbs.
stories.impact: Healthy bid volume on older garden-style product in St. Louis metro suggests robust buyer demand for sub-$500K/unit assets with solid operations, indicating development of workforce/Class B+/C products remains viable in Midwest submits. Competitive bidding may support cap rates and exit assumptions for similar vintage properties under development.

stories.title: Kolter, BH Inch Toward Buyout on Oceanfront Miami Beach Condo
stories.excerpt: Developers Kolter Group and BH Group are almost done assembling their oceanfront site in Miami Beach, with plans to redevelop it into a luxury condo complex. The joint venture now owns the majority of units within the Port Royale condo building at 6969 Collins Avenue in the North Beach neighborhood. Since July, it has paid $61.6 million for 163 units within the 172-unit building, according to an analysis of property records by data company Vizzda, first reported by the Business Journals. Five years ago, Port Royale residents were evacuated after the 55-year-old building was deemed unsafe, CBS Miami reported. The evacuation came after the deadly collapse of the nearby Champlain Towers South condo building in 2021. The condo sales are likely related to state reforms passed after 2021 that have increased building maintenance fees for many condo owners, some of whom are selling to developers. The recent purchases add to Kolter Group and BH Group’s assemblage, which spans about 2 acres along the oceanfront between 69th and 71st streets and includes two neighboring hotels. Starting in 2023, Kolter purchased the 34,980-square-foot Normandy Plaza Hotel for $18 million. Located at 6985 Collins Avenue, the three-story structure was built in 1950. This January, an entity tied to the joint venture paid $26 million for the four-story Crystal Beach Suites, which was built in 1936 at 6979 Collins Avenue. This July, it also purchased the 7,600-square-foot commercial condos within the building for $14.4 million. This week, Wells Fargo increased a loan tied to those properties to $83.2 million. The bank doubled the debt amount from a mortgage first issued in January. Last week, the developers filed plans to demolish the Normandy Plaza Hotel. In 2025, they filed plans to build a 37-unit condo development designed by Kobi Karp on a portion of the site. bullets: Kolter Group + BH Group bought 163 of 172 units in Port Royale condo (Miami Beach) for $61.6M since July
Building vacated 2021 post-Champlain Towers collapse; state building reform raised condo fees
JV acquiring inventory toward full redevelopment into luxury condo complex
stories.summary: Kolter Group and BH Group are assembling Port Royale, a 172-unit condo building at 6969 Collins Avenue in Miami Beach's North Beach, purchasing 163 units for $61.6 million since July. The 55-year-old building was evacuated after the 2021 Champlain Towers South collapse; state post-collapse reforms increased condo maintenance fees, prompting owner sales to the developers. The joint venture plans a complete redevelopment into a luxury condo property.
stories.impact: Post-Champlain regulatory burden (mandatory reserve studies, higher maintenance) is forcing condo owner exits in prime oceanfront Miami locations, creating opportunistic assembly plays for major developers. Regulatory-driven distress in condo buildings is accelerating redevelopment and conversion to new luxury product, reshaping North Beach supply and pulling capital from older inventory.

stories.title: Olnick Organization Refinances Harlem Apartments for $171M
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop arranged $170.5 million in permanent financing to refinance Lenox Terrace, a multifamily community at 484 Malcolm X Blvd. in Harlem. A Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory team led by Jonathan Schwartz, Aaron Appel, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer, Michael Ianno and Cody Ela arranged the balance sheet financing from Chase Commercial Bank on behalf of The Olnick Organization. The new financing is on a cash-neutral basis to retire the existing loan. “Lenox Terrace combines a scale, location, and operating history that are difficult to replicate in Manhattan,” said Jonathan Schwartz, senior managing director and co-head of Capital Markets Institutional Advisory at Walker & Dunlop. “Against a backdrop of limited new multifamily supply in New York City, the property represents a substantial concentration of well-located, primarily rent-regulated rental housing. We’re grateful to The Olnick Organization and Chase Commercial Bank for their partnership in arranging a financing that supports the property’s long-term strategy.” Originally developed in 1958, Lenox Terrace features 1,696 primarily rent-regulated residences across six 16-story buildings. The post Olnick Organization Refinances Harlem Apartments for $171M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Olnick Organization refi'd Lenox Terrace (1,696 units, Harlem, NYC) for $170.5M via Chase
Primarily rent-regulated asset; built 1958, six 16-story buildings on Malcolm X Blvd
Cash-neutral refi reflects stability of rent-regulated anchors in supply-constrained Manhattan
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop arranged a $170.5 million permanent refinancing for Lenox Terrace, a 1,696-unit rent-regulated multifamily community in Harlem built in 1958. Chase Commercial Bank provided the institutional financing on a cash-neutral basis. The deal underscores the strategic value of large, stabilized rent-regulated portfolios in a market with severely constrained new supply.
stories.impact: Strong refinancing of a major rent-regulated platform in Manhattan signals lender confidence in long-term cash flows from regulated housing and the scarcity premium on large, well-located rent-regulated stock. Limited new supply in NYC makes existing rent-regulated mega-assets increasingly valuable for long-hold institutional investors, supporting high leverage and favorable terms.

stories.title: Newmark Arranges $31M Sale of Advanced Manufacturing Campus in Hillsboro
stories.excerpt: Newmark has arranged the $30.9 million sale of Trellis West, a 214,152-square-foot advanced manufacturing and research and development campus in Hillsboro, Oregon, to buyer SKB and KCB Partners. Newmark Director Kellen Kollmorgen represented the seller in the transaction. Leasing efforts at Trellis West were led by Newmark Portland Market Leader and Managing Director Travis Parrott and Managing Director Josh Schweitz. Newmark’s Western Region Capital Markets group leveraged its client relationships to bring this transaction to fruition, with support from group President and Executive Vice Chairman Steve Golubchik and Senior Managing Director Darren Hollak. Golubchik leads strategy for the group, which includes Kollmorgen. Currently 90% leased, Trellis West is a four-building campus anchored by semiconductor industry leaders Applied Materials and KLA. Parrott and Schweitz began leasing advisory services for Trellis West in May 2025 to help stabilize the property, securing nearly 87,000 square feet across five separate leases at market-high rents. In addition to KLA, the team has landed commitments from SemiAnalysis, Chempower Corporation, Onto Innovation and Hyve Solutions. The post Newmark Arranges $31M Sale of Advanced Manufacturing Campus in Hillsboro appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trellis West (214K SF advanced manufacturing campus, Hillsboro, OR) sold for $30.9M to SKB/KCB
Currently 90% leased; anchored by Applied Materials and KLA semiconductor leaders
Newmark secured ~87K SF new leases at market-high rents during 2025 stabilization effort
stories.summary: Newmark arranged the $30.9 million sale of Trellis West, a 214,152-square-foot advanced manufacturing and R&D campus in Hillsboro, Oregon, anchored by semiconductor equipment leaders Applied Materials and KLA. The property is 90% leased; Newmark's leasing team secured nearly 87,000 square feet across five new leases at elevated rents in 2025. The sale captures strong occupancy and robust demand from semiconductor supply-chain tenants.
stories.impact: Active leasing momentum and market-rate rents for semiconductor-adjacent industrial space in Portland's Hillsboro submarket (Intel corridor) reflect continued strength in chip equipment and advanced manufacturing clusters. High occupancy and pricing support continued speculative and build-to-suit development of industrial/R&D product targeting semiconductor supply-chain tenants in the region.

stories.title: Google Relocation Leads D.C.’s Office Market in Q3
stories.excerpt: Washington, D.C.’s office market held relatively steady in the third quarter, but the divide between trophy properties and the broader market was extended. Tenants leased about 1.8 million square feet during the quarter, roughly in line with the market’s five-year quarterly average, but down from the 2 million square feet leased in the second quarter, according to Savills. Overall availability ticked down to 24 percent, while trophy space availability remained below 10 percent. The average Class A asking rent inched up 2 pennies since the second quarter to $62.31 per square foot per year. That scarcity in premier space is prompting tenants — mostly law firms and government departments — to make decisions years ahead of lease expirations while encouraging landlords to reposition buildings, according to Savills. Sheppard signed the quarter’s largest law firm deal, relocating to 107,227 square feet at 2033 K Street NW, where the property is slated for an extensive redevelopment. Greenberg Traurig also renewed and expanded to 80,089 square feet at 2101 L Street NW. Google posted the quarter’s largest lease deal in a 210,000-square-foot consolidation move to 500 North Capitol Street NW. And the local D.C. government renewed for 164,110 square feet at 1050 First Street NE and for 74,924 square feet at 645 H Street NE both ranked among the quarter’s largest deals. Federal leasing, however, remains a weak spot. Savills said General Services Administration leasing volume is on pace to decline from 2025 with fewer transactions above 100,000 square feet through the first three quarters. Meanwhile, D.C.’s office inventory declined by 4.7 million square feet compared to the same time last year, falling to 118.1 million square feet, as office-to-resi conversions continue removing space from the market. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: D.C. office: 1.8M SF leased Q3 (vs. 2M SF Q2), five-year average on track
Class A trophy availability <10%; overall availability 24%; Class A rents $62.31/SF/year
Google relocation and law firm consolidation driving trophy tenant demand; repos accelerating
stories.summary: Washington, D.C.'s office market posted 1.8 million square feet of leasing in Q3 2024, roughly in line with the five-year quarterly average but down from Q2's 2 million square feet, per Savills. Trophy space availability remained below 10% while overall market availability sat at 24%; Class A asking rents edged up to $62.31 per square foot annually. Tenants—primarily law firms and government departments—are committing years early to secure premier space, spurring landlord repositioning.
stories.impact: Extreme scarcity in Class A trophy space is driving early commitment cycles and accelerating repositioning deals (e.g., 2033 K Street redevelopment), but broader market softness and high overall availability limit development upside. Multifamily developers should note that office repositioning and mixed-use redevelopment may accelerate in D.C.'s core, competing for land and capital, while tenant consolidation into trophy properties continues to hollow out secondary/tertiary office stock.

stories.title: Bank of America, JLL Provide $276M Refi for SoCal Senior Housing
stories.excerpt: A Nexus Development affiliate has landed $276 million in refinancing for two senior housing communities with 395 units in Newport Beach, Calif. Property records show that Bank of America provided the $140 million loan for Vivante Newport Center, while JLL Real Estate Capital provided $136 million for Vivante Newport Mesa. JLL Capital Markets arranged and announced the financings for the owner on Friday, but declined to identify the lenders. The $140 million loan for the 99-unit Newport Center loan works out to roughly $1.4 million per unit, which is one of the largest financings on a per-unit basis in the senior housing industry’s history, according to JLL. The six-story property opened in 2022 on San Clemente Drive with restaurants, a cocktail bar, a fitness center, an indoor pool, a theater, a bowling alley and a golf simulator. It is also near Fashion Island and Hoag Hospital Newport Beach. Meanwhile, Vivante Newport Mesa includes 296 units across a 6.8-acre campus on Monrovia Avenue. The property opened in phases in 2013 and 2020 with a three-story building and a four-story building. It is near South Coast Plaza. JLL’s Greg Brown and Aaron Rosenzweig represented privately held developer Nexus Development. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bank of America + JLL refi'd $276M for two senior housing properties, Newport Beach, CA
Vivante Newport Center (99 units, 2022): $140M (~$1.4M/unit); Newport Mesa (296 units): $136M
Luxury senior housing showing strong lender appetite and record-tier per-unit debt capacity
stories.summary: Bank of America and JLL provided $276 million in refinancing for two Nexus Development-affiliated senior housing communities totaling 395 units in Newport Beach, California. The $140 million financing for the 99-unit Vivante Newport Center (opened 2022) equates to roughly $1.4 million per unit, among the highest on record for senior housing. Vivante Newport Mesa (296 units, 2013/2020) secured $136 million.
stories.impact: Refinancing at $1.4M per unit for new luxury senior housing validates aggressive underwriting for upscale independent/assisted living in high-net-worth coastal markets. Strong institutional lender appetite suggests development pipeline will continue to favor luxury senior housing in affluent submarkets over value/workforce products.

stories.title: Sony in Talks to Anchor Tishman Speyer’s 99 Hudson Boulevard
stories.excerpt: Sony is in negotiations to become the anchor tenant of Tishman Speyer’s planned 99 Hudson Boulevard in Hudson Yards, Commercial Observer has learned, and may already have a term sheet. Sony’s current U.S. headquarters is in the top 568,000 square feet of 11 Madison Avenue, but Sony, like other corporate occupiers, is looking for newer, bigger and more collaborative workplaces for its employees. Sony signed a lease in 2013 and moved to 11 Madison after selling its iconic 550 Madison Avenue headquarters in 2012 to Joseph Chetrit for $1.12 billion. Chetrit flipped it three years later for $1.4 billion to Olayan America, which completely redeveloped the tower, which features a distinctive Chippendale-style top designed by Philip Johnson and John Burgee. While Sony’s current location in vibrant NoMad next to Madison Square Park is hard to beat, there is simply no room to expand in the 30-story building. It was originally designed by Harvey Wiley Corbett and Dan Everett Wade in 1928 to hit 100 stories before the Great Depression stopped its ascent. The Art Deco tower was not completed until 1950 and is currently owned by SL Green Realty. It’s unclear how much space Sony is in talks for at 99 Hudson Boulevard. Savills’ Erik Schmall and Allyson Bowen are representing Sony in the negotiations, but did not respond to requests for comment. Tishman Speyer has proposed 99 Hudson Boulevard as a 48-story office building of roughly 1.256 million square feet. Public documents state the firm will start construction on Dec. 1. The planned tower will sit opposite the Javits Center on 11th Avenue between West 36th and West 37th streets and have unobstructed views of the Hudson River. Its primary address of 99 Hudson Boulevard would place its main lobby facing the new Bella Abzug Park. Constructed as an all-electric LEED Gold tower, it would not be ready for occupancy until around 2030. bullets: Sony in talks to anchor Tishman Speyer's 99 Hudson Boulevard (Hudson Yards, Manhattan)
Sony currently at 11 Madison Avenue (568K SF); seeking larger, newer collaborative space
Major corporate tenant seeking modern office signals continued Hudson Yards demand and lease activity
stories.summary: Sony is negotiating to become the anchor tenant at Tishman Speyer's 99 Hudson Boulevard development in Hudson Yards, Manhattan, per Commercial Observer. Sony occupies 568,000 square feet atop 11 Madison Avenue in NoMad but seeks larger, newer office with better collaborative workspace. The company sold its 550 Madison Avenue flagship in 2012 and relocated in 2013.
stories.impact: Major Sony lease to new Hudson Yards office confirms continued institutional tenant demand for modern, amenity-rich office in Manhattan's trophy markets; however, this is an office story with minimal multifamily relevance. Indirectly, sustained office demand in Hudson Yards may support surrounding mixed-use and residential development, but the article signals office, not residential, market traction.

stories.title: Hines Promotes Adam Hines to Co-CEO Alongside Laura Hines-Pierce
stories.excerpt: Laura Hines-Pierce is still co-CEO of the family firm, but with a new counterpart in Adam Hines. Hines-Pierce ascended to the role of co-CEO of investment and development firm Hines in February 2022 alongside her father, Jeffrey Hines. But as the elder Hines moves into the role of the firm’s chairman, another family member is moving up. Effective Jan. 1, Adam Hines and Hines-Pierce will lead the day-to-day operations of the company and strategic trajectory in the years to come, according to Hines. In addition, Hines-Pierce will replace Jeffrey Hines as CEO and chair of the board of Hines Global Income Trust, while Adam Hines will join its board as a director. “Hines has always been at its best when we look beyond the current cycle and build for what comes next,” Jeffrey Hines said in a statement. “Laura has already been leading Hines as co-CEO for five years, and Adam has helped shape important parts of our growth across Europe, private wealth and capital formation. Their leadership is already visible in the firm and platform we have built.” Also switching up their roles at Hines are David Steinbach, who was promoted to become the firm’s first president, and Alfonso Munk, who was promoted from co-head of investment management and will replace Steinbach as Hines’ global chief investment officer. “Scale creates advantage only when it improves execution,” Steinbach said in a statement. “Our opportunity is to connect what our teams know across markets, strategies and functions so local insight becomes shared intelligence and firmwide capabilities create more opportunity on the ground.” Adam Hines was recognized for doubling Hines’ private wealth business during his time as chief of staff for the office of the CEO and senior managing director of the company. He joined Hines in 2017 after holding several analyst positions at Australian real assets management firm Dexus. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Hines promotes Adam Hines to co-CEO (Jan 1, 2025) alongside Laura Hines-Pierce
Jeffrey Hines (founder) transitions to chairman; Laura named CEO/chair of Hines Global Income Trust
Leadership succession at major global developer; no direct impact on pipeline or markets
stories.summary: Hines announced a leadership succession effective January 1, 2025: Adam Hines and Laura Hines-Pierce will serve as co-CEOs managing day-to-day operations, while Jeffrey Hines transitions to chairman. Laura Hines-Pierce will also assume the CEO and board chair role of Hines Global Income Trust, while Adam joins its board. The move consolidates next-generation family leadership across the firm's investment and development platform.
stories.impact: Internal leadership transition at Hines has minimal bearing on multifamily demand, supply, capital availability, or construction costs. No market-specific impact or change in strategic direction is disclosed; this is administrative/governance news with no second-order market effect.
